correctness.rationale: Coarea makes diagonal section area sqrt(n)*f_n(t); maximal in-cube vertex height is (n/2+t)/sqrt(n), hence volume (n/2+t)f_n(t)/n. Positive log concavity of the centered Irwin–Hall density and strict log concavity of n/2+t imply a unique optimum t_n>0. Fourier inversion with log sinc=-s^2/24-s^4/2880-s^6/181440+... gives uniform compact-t expansions of f_n and derivative. Independently recomputed rational Gaussian moments to verify coefficients -3/20,-13/1120, 2/45,7/120,73/3360, and numerical Irwin–Hall maxima for n=3,5,10,25,100; for n=3 t=(sqrt2-1)/2, D=(1+sqrt2)/6. Numerical checks do not prove the high-dimensional uniform errors; the analytic Gaussian tail controls are the proof.
